transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess I'm here because... well, I've just been in a bit of a slump lately. I really don't want to sound lazy or anything, but I just don't seem to care about much anymore. 

I used to do a lot—I had my art classes, and I'd go to board-game nights with people. I loved hiking, too, and I was supposed to be getting back to my soccer team. But lately, I just... I don't know, I can't bring myself to care about any of it. I feel awful admitting it, because I know I should be out there doing things, but I just end up sitting in my room while everything sort of slips away from me. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be trying harder to keep up with my life. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, well... I guess it's been quite a while. It's a little embarrassing to admit, because I really thought I would have bounced back by now, but... it started shortly after my divorce. That was about, um, a year and eleven months ago. 

I know that sounds like a really long time to still be stuck in a rut like this, and I'm sorry, I really have been trying to pull myself together. I just haven't been doing a very good job of it. Is... is that the kind of timeline you needed to know?
Do you still enjoy things you used to like, or has the pleasure gone away as well?

Um, yeah... like I mentioned earlier, I really just don't care about anything anymore. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. But, um, yeah, the pleasure really is just... gone. 

Even with the things I brought up before, like my art classes or the board-game nights, or hiking. I used to get so much joy out of those, and I really wanted to get back to my soccer team. But now, even if I try to think about doing them, I just feel... empty about it? I end up just sitting in my room, and I know I shouldn't. I know I should be making more of an effort to be positive and active, but I just sort of sit there while everything slips away. 

I really wish I could still enjoy those things, because I don't want to be a burden or seem ungrateful for the life I have. I hope it's okay that I'm explaining it this way... does that answer your question alright?
Have you had any periods in the past year where you felt really good, like your normal self, without these feelings of emptiness and lack of interest?

Um... I really wish I could say yes, because I want to give you a better answer. I know I should be having good days. But... no, I haven't really felt like myself at all in the past year. 

Things kind of fluctuated at first, but it really became... well, constant, I guess, around the following summer. So it's been just this steady feeling for about a year and four months now. I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible, and I really have been trying my hardest to snap out of it so I can be normal again. I just haven't been able to shake it since that summer. 

I hope I'm not being too negative by saying that... is that the right kind of information you needed?
Have you been experiencing any feelings of worry or fear that are overwhelming or difficult to control?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I guess everyone worries a little bit, right? But I wouldn't say it's overwhelming or anything like that. 

I really don't want to make it sound like I'm anxious on top of everything else. I know I'm already dealing with so much, and I don't want to be complicated or difficult to treat. So, um, no, I don't think I have those kinds of fears or anything that I can't control. I just feel mostly... down, like I was saying before. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm not confusing things for you.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

Um, well... I know we just talked about this a little bit, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm not trying. I know I should be finding things to enjoy. But... no, not really. 

Like I mentioned, the things I used to love—my art classes, the board-game nights, hiking, even the idea of getting back on my soccer team... I just don't care about them anymore. I really wish I did, because I know it would be better for me, but I just end up sitting in my room instead. I feel like everything is just kind of slipping away while I sit there. 

I'm so sorry if that's not what you were hoping to hear. I really am trying to be cooperative... is it okay that I don't have anything I enjoy right now?
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you were dead?

Um... well... I know this is one of those questions where there's a right answer and a wrong answer, and I really don't want to worry you or make you think I'm, you know, a danger or anything. I really don't want to be a burden. 

But... I guess I should be honest, right? Because I want you to be able to help me. Um... sometimes... I just keep having these thoughts that I don't want to wake up anymore. It's not that I want to do anything bad, I just... I get so tired. 

And, um, there was this one time recently... my friend came over and found me, and I guess I had been saying out loud that I couldn't keep living like this. I didn't even realize I was doing it, and I felt so terrible for scaring her. I really didn't mean to. 

I'm so sorry if that's upsetting to hear. I promise I'm trying to hold on. Is... is it okay that I told you that? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Um... well, I really don't want to make a big deal out of it. I know you're probably asking because you want to make sure I'm taking care of myself, and I promise I'm trying to be good about that. I really am. 

But... I guess I have lost a little bit of weight. It's just... I go most of the day without eating lately. I try, but food just tastes like cardboard to me right now. I didn't even really notice the weight loss at first, but my jeans have gotten so loose that I actually have to knot the waistband to keep them up. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be eating better. I don't want you to think I'm neglecting myself on purpose or trying to be difficult. I'll try to do better, I promise. Does that... does that answer your question okay?
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or the way you move?

Um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything, because I know everyone gets tired sometimes. I'm really trying to push through it. 

But... yeah, I guess there have been some changes. Sometimes I feel so heavy, like... moving just takes so much effort. Even just trying to make a cup of coffee feels like I'm trying to lift wet cement. I move so slowly, and I know it probably looks awful, and I'm sorry if I'm not being as active as I should be.

And then... other times, it's like the opposite? I get this weird energy, but not a good kind. I'll just pace back and forth, from the kitchen to the window, over and over until my legs actually ache. I try to stop, I really do, because I know it's probably weird to watch, but I just can't settle down. 

I hope that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling heavy and moving slowly, is that something that happens all the time or does it come and go?

Um... well, it definitely comes and goes. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, because I know I need to be more consistent. I try so hard to be. 

But, um... yeah, it's not all the time. Like I was saying, there are days where I just... I move so slowly, and my arms and legs feel so heavy, like that wet cement feeling when I'm just trying to make coffee. And I feel awful because I know I should be getting things done. 

And then... other days, it's that pacing thing. I'll just walk back and forth, kitchen to the window, kitchen to the window, until my legs literally ache. It's like I can't find a middle ground, and I'm really sorry if that sounds confusing. I'm trying to manage it better, I promise. Does that... does that help explain it a little better?
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed most of the day?

Um... well, I really don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. I know I should be looking on the bright side, and I really try to be positive, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm not trying.

But... um, yeah. I guess it's been going on for a while now, definitely more than two weeks. It's just... most days, I wake up and I just have this really heavy, hollow feeling right here in my chest. It's like... like there's just no future for me outside of my apartment walls. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so dramatic and negative. I really don't mean to be a downer, and I'm trying to snap out of it, I really am. I just... I can't seem to shake that feeling lately. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Are there any small things that still bring you some joy or pleasure?

Um... I really wish I could say yes. I know I should have hobbies and things that keep me busy. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or being lazy, because I know how important it is to stay active. 

But... honestly, no. I just... I don't care about anything anymore. I used to love my art classes, and I'd go to board-game nights with friends... I even liked hiking and I was hoping to get back on my recreational soccer team. I know I should still be doing those things, and I feel terrible that I'm letting everyone down by not showing up. 

Now I just... I just sit in my room. It feels like everything is just slipping away from me, and I can't even find the energy to care about it. I'm so sorry, I know that's not what you want to hear, and I know I need to try harder to find things I enjoy. I really am trying to be better about it. Is it bad that I've let all those things go?
Do you feel like you're at the worst point you've ever been in your life right now?

Um... well, I really don't want to complain. I know there are people who have it so much worse than I do, and I'm really lucky to have a roof over my head and, you know, just the basics. I don't want to sound ungrateful at all. 

But... um, I don't know if it's the absolute worst it's ever been. It's definitely really hard right now, but I'm trying to keep things in perspective. I know I just need to push through this rough patch and stop feeling so sorry for myself. I promise I'm really working on being stronger. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm not taking this seriously.
Have you experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others cannot?

Um... oh gosh. I really, really don't want you to think I'm crazy, or... or that I'm making things up for attention. I know how bad this is going to sound, and I've been trying so hard to just ignore it and be rational, I promise I have. 

But... um, yeah. Sometimes... I do hear something. It's... it's a woman's voice. She usually talks to me from the corner of my room. She tells me that... well, she says that I ruined everything, and that I should just stay inside. And the thing is, it's not just like a thought in my head. It sounds as clear as someone standing right next to my bed. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds really alarming, and I don't want to worry you or be a burden. I'm probably just letting my stress get the best of me, right? I really am trying to push it away and just be normal. Is it... is it okay that I'm telling you this? I hope I'm not making things too difficult by bringing it up.
Do the voices you hear comment on your actions or thoughts, or do they tell you to do or not do specific things?

Um... well, she doesn't really comment on every little thing I do, if that's what you mean. I know some people hear voices that narrate their whole day, and I'm really glad it's not like that for me. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. 

It's mostly just... like I said, she tells me I ruined everything. And she does tell me what to do, but it's really just that one thing. She tells me I should stay inside. That's usually what she says when she's talking from the corner of my room. 

I really try not to listen to her, though. I know she's not real, even if she sounds exactly like someone standing right next to my bed. I know I shouldn't let it keep me from doing things, and I'm trying really hard to just ignore her and push past it. I hope you don't think I'm just using it as an excuse to isolate myself. I'm doing the right thing by trying to ignore it, aren't I?
Do the voices you hear ever tell you to harm yourself or others?

Oh! No, no, definitely not. Um... I really want to make sure you know that. She never says anything violent like that. I would never want to hurt anyone, or... or myself. I promise. I know how important it is to be safe, and I'm really trying to be good about all of this. 

It's really just the... the staying inside thing, like I mentioned. I really hope you don't think I'm dangerous or a threat to anyone just because I'm hearing her. I'm not, I swear. I would tell you right away if she ever said something scary like that, because I want to do exactly what I'm supposed to do to get better. I'm doing the right thing by being honest with you about this, right? I just really don't want you to worry about me being unsafe.
Do you think the voice you hear is related to your feelings of sadness and emptiness?

Um... I guess so? I mean, I really don't want to make it sound like I'm just wallowing in it or anything, but... yeah, they do seem to happen together a lot. 

For, um, for much of this past year, the... the low mood and the voices have been happening at the same time. Like, I would be lying in bed, just feeling so incredibly hopeless and empty, and... and that's when I'd be hearing that woman telling me I ruined everything. 

I know I shouldn't let myself get that down, and I really am trying to stay positive. It's just hard when she's right there, you know? But I'm not trying to use her as an excuse for being sad. I hope it's okay that I'm explaining it this way... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me. Is that... is that the kind of connection you were asking about?
Have you experienced any significant impairment in your social, occupational, or other areas of functioning due to your depressive symptoms?

Um... well... I don't want to make it sound like I'm completely falling apart or anything. I know I need to be trying harder to keep up with things. But... yeah, it has been really hard lately. 

I haven't been taking on any of my freelance art-education work for a while now. I just... I don't want to let anyone down by doing a bad job, you know? And I've been skipping out on community events, and my soccer games... which I feel terrible about. I really do want to go, I just can't seem to get myself out the door. 

And, um... my friend has been coming over to check on me a lot. I'm really lucky to have her, but I feel so guilty that she has to do it. I just haven't been very good at... well, remembering to eat, or shower regularly. And she just wants to make sure I'm safe and taking care of myself. I know I should be able to do those things on my own, and I'm really trying to get back on track. I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or giving up. I'm doing the right thing by letting my friend help me for now, aren't I?
Do you think your symptoms are significantly interfering with your daily life, making it hard for you to function normally?

Um... I mean, I guess it is, yeah. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or just giving up, because I'm not. I'm really trying my best to keep it together. But... I suppose it is interfering a lot right now. 

Like I was saying, I've completely stopped taking on any of my freelance art-education work. I just... I don't want to disappoint any of the kids or the programs if I can't do a good job. And I've missed all the community events I usually help with, and my soccer games. I feel awful about letting my team down, I really do. 

And... well, I guess the biggest thing is that I really do need my friend coming over to check on me. I hate being a burden to her, but... I'm just not doing a very good job of reliably eating, or showering, or... or even just making sure I'm staying safe on my own. I know I should be handling all of this better at my age, and I really want to get back to normal. It's okay that I'm letting her help me while things are so hard, right? I'm just trying to make sure I don't let things get even worse.
Do you feel like your symptoms are severe enough that you're unable to do even the smallest tasks without feeling overwhelmed?

Um... I really hate to admit this, because I know how bad it sounds. I promise I'm not trying to just be lazy, and I know I should be pushing myself harder. But... yes, it really does feel that way. 

Like, even after I’ve been in bed for half the day—and I know I shouldn't be doing that, I really am trying to get up earlier—but even with all that rest, just... taking a shower, or even answering one single text message from my friend... it honestly feels like I’ve already worked a full shift. It just takes everything out of me. 

I feel so silly getting so overwhelmed by such tiny things. I really don't want you to think I'm just making excuses. It's... it's okay that I'm struggling with this right now, isn't it? I'm trying my best to push through it, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how exhausting everything feels... does that make sense?
